title: Mac Storage Audit

items.name: Xcode build cache
items.note: Xcode rebuilds it on the next build. That first build is slower.

items.name: Old iPhone debug symbols (9 of 11 iOS versions)
items.note: Keeps the newest 2. Xcode copies symbols again if you plug in a phone on an older version.
items.cmd: delete every version folder except the newest 2

items.name: Simulator system caches
items.note: Rebuilt the next time a simulator boots.

items.name: Developer and app caches
items.note: Yarn 7.9, Chrome 6.7, Playwright 2.5, Cypress 2.3, CocoaPods 1.7, Spotify 1.6, Go 1.5, pnpm 1.1, Homebrew 0.7 GB. Cypress and Playwright download their browsers again on the next test run.

items.name: Project build output
items.note: Gitignored android/app/build, Pods, dist, .gradle and .next folders. Biggest: mobile-app Android build 9.7 GB, shop-app Android build 4.6 GB. Pods come back with `pod install`.
items.cmd: find_build_dirs.sh, then delete the deletable rows

items.name: pnpm package store
items.note: Prune removes only packages that no project on disk uses.

items.name: uv Python package cache
items.note: Python packages download again on the next install.

items.name: node_modules in 207 project folders
items.note: Biggest: mobile-app 13.8, shop-app 7.7, wallet-app 5.4, budget-app 2.9 GB. An install restores it.

items.name: Simulator devices (113)
items.note: Deleting a simulator deletes the apps and data inside it. Xcode recreates the default set.

items.name: Old iOS simulator runtimes (5 of 7)
items.note: Keeps the newest iOS 26 and one iOS 18. Xcode → Settings → Components downloads any of them again.

items.name: Hugging Face models
items.note: Models download again the next time a script asks for them.

items.name: OrbStack containers and images
items.note: Not running now. Prune unused images and volumes from inside OrbStack.

items.name: Docker Desktop disk
items.note: Last used two months ago and not running. If OrbStack replaced it, this can go.

items.name: Android emulator
items.note: Wipe Data shrinks it. Delete it if you test on a real device.

items.name: WhatsApp media
items.note: Photos, videos and voice notes from chats.

items.name: CapCut projects
items.note: Video projects.

items.name: Chrome profile data
items.note: History, extensions and site storage. Clear it from inside Chrome only.

items.name: Claude desktop VM bundles
items.note: Downloaded again if missing. Leave it unless space is tight.

items.name: Cursor app data
items.note: Workspace state and chat history.

items.name: Xcode Archives (32 builds)
items.note: Needed to read crash reports for shipped builds, unless the dSYMs are uploaded.

items.name: Video edits
items.note: Exported or in-progress edits.

items.name: Genymotion virtual devices
items.note: Delete unused devices from Genymotion.

items.name: promo-reel build folder
items.note: Probably a bundle that rebuilds. Check it for rendered videos first.

keep.name: macOS system volumes
keep.detail: System, Preboot, Recovery and VM · 22 GB

keep.name: Installed apps
keep.detail: `/Applications` · 23 GB. Uninstall apps you don't use rather than deleting their parts.

keep.name: Other app data
keep.detail: Application Support, Containers and Group Containers for apps not listed above.

keep.name: OrbStack's disk image file
keep.detail: `data.img.raw`. Clean OrbStack from inside the app.

notes: About 66 GB didn't show up in the scan. The terminal can't read Mail, Messages, Photos or Safari data without Full Disk Access.
Sizes are binary gigabytes, as `du` and `df` report them. Finder shows about 7% more.
`~/Library/GroupContainersAlias` is a shortcut to Group Containers. Tools that follow it count the same data twice.
Close Xcode, the simulators, Docker and OrbStack before their folders are cleaned.
questions: Is Docker Desktop still in use, or did OrbStack replace it?
Which projects are active? Only inactive ones should lose node_modules.
Do you still test on iOS 18? That decides which simulator runtimes stay.
Do you still use the Android emulator and Genymotion?
Are dSYMs uploaded, so old archives can go?
